questions.q: How does the editorial describe dawah?
options: A contest to prove one’s faith superior
Not quite. The article says: A peaceful, two-way sharing of what one has found, in which each also learns from the other.
A peaceful, two-way sharing of what one has found, in which each also learns from the other
Yes. It is not debate, and nothing is imposed.
A campaign to change other people’s religion
Not quite. The article says: A peaceful, two-way sharing of what one has found, in which each also learns from the other.
A set of rules for new believers
Not quite. The article says: A peaceful, two-way sharing of what one has found, in which each also learns from the other.
questions.rationale: “Dawah is a bilateral process which involves sharing of thoughts… Contrary to imposing one’s ideas on others, it stands for sharing one’s discovery with others.”

questions.q: According to the editorial, who is involved when a person adopts a faith?
options: The religious authorities
Not quite. The article says: Only the person himself and his Creator; it is his own free discovery.
Only the person himself and his Creator; it is his own free discovery
Right. There is no “converter.”
His family and community
Not quite. The article says: Only the person himself and his Creator; it is his own free discovery.
The preacher who persuaded him
Not quite. The article says: Only the person himself and his Creator; it is his own free discovery.
questions.rationale: “When a person accepts a faith different from his previous faith, he alone should make the choice on the basis of his discovery… there is no one in between him and His Creator.”

questions.article: War Is No Choice at All
questions.q: Why, according to the article, does war not end when one side defeats the other?
options: Treaties are never written down
Not quite. The article says: The defeated side does not accept defeat and is overtaken by a thirst for revenge.
Weapons are too easily bought
Not quite. The article says: The defeated side does not accept defeat and is overtaken by a thirst for revenge.
The defeated side does not accept defeat and is overtaken by a thirst for revenge
Yes. So the problem returns in a worse form.
The victors always quarrel among themselves
Not quite. The article says: The defeated side does not accept defeat and is overtaken by a thirst for revenge.
questions.rationale: “War cannot cease by one party defeating another. In practice, what happens is that the defeated party does not accept its defeat. Instead, a thirst for revenge overtakes it.”

questions.q: What outlook does the article recommend to a newly married couple?
options: To see each other’s different qualities as complementary, and adjust instead of complaining
Yes. Differences are part of the Creator’s plan.
To avoid discussing anything difficult
Not quite. The article says: To see each other’s different qualities as complementary, and adjust instead of complaining.
To make sure one of them always decides
Not quite. The article says: To see each other’s different qualities as complementary, and adjust instead of complaining.
To live as far as possible like their parents
Not quite. The article says: To see each other’s different qualities as complementary, and adjust instead of complaining.
questions.rationale: “Women and men are not opposing genders, but complement each other… they will acknowledge and appreciate each other, instead of complaining and clashing.”

questions.q: What does the article say a habit of listening more than speaking reveals about a person?
options: Sincerity and humility – the essence of a fine character
Correct. Much talk often means self-praise.
Indifference to others
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity and humility – the essence of a fine character.
A wish to hide one’s views
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity and humility – the essence of a fine character.
Shyness and lack of knowledge
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity and humility – the essence of a fine character.
questions.rationale: “The practice of listening more than speaking… reflects rather a whole state of mind. Indicative of sincerity and humility, it is the essence of a fine character.”

questions.q: The deposed King Faruq joked that soon only five kings would remain – four in a pack of cards and the King of England. What does the article admire in him?
options: He plotted patiently to return
Not quite. The article says: He understood the change of the age and accepted his loss, sparing himself bitterness.
He blamed his ministers
Not quite. The article says: He understood the change of the age and accepted his loss, sparing himself bitterness.
He understood the change of the age and accepted his loss, sparing himself bitterness
Well read. He lived on peacefully.
He refused to leave his country
Not quite. The article says: He understood the change of the age and accepted his loss, sparing himself bitterness.
questions.rationale: “Acknowledging the end of dynastic rule, he was able to take his forced abdication as inevitable… he saved himself from negative thinking.”

questions.q: A disciple of Ibn Abbas explained the “worship” for which man was created (Quran 51:56). In what terms?
options: As the performance of fixed rituals
Not quite. The article says: As the realisation, or discovery, of God.
As withdrawal from the world
Not quite. The article says: As the realisation, or discovery, of God.
As obedience to rulers
Not quite. The article says: As the realisation, or discovery, of God.
As the realisation, or discovery, of God
Yes. Truth found by one’s own reflection.
questions.rationale: “Mujaahid… has explained worshipping God in terms of the realization of God… Realization or Maarifat means the discovery of God.”

questions.article: The Difference Between a Believer and an Unbeliever
questions.q: On his death-bed the Caliph Umar asked his son to rest his cheek on the dust. What contrast does the article draw from this?
options: Rulers should be buried without honours
Not quite. The article says: The believer humbles himself before God in this life, unseen; others will do so only when they see Him.
The believer humbles himself before God in this life, unseen; others will do so only when they see Him
Exactly. Only the first has merit.
The strong fear death more than the weak
Not quite. The article says: The believer humbles himself before God in this life, unseen; others will do so only when they see Him.
The old are wiser than the young
Not quite. The article says: The believer humbles himself before God in this life, unseen; others will do so only when they see Him.
questions.rationale: “An unbeliever will humble himself on seeing God: a believer does so without seeing Him.”

questions.q: In place of “The sky is the limit,” what guide does the article propose?
options: Aim low so as never to fail
Not quite. The article says: Work to the full, but when stress sets in, recognise that your natural limit has been reached.
Work to the full, but when stress sets in, recognise that your natural limit has been reached
Right. Limits are marked by peace of mind.
Let others set your limits
Not quite. The article says: Work to the full, but when stress sets in, recognise that your natural limit has been reached.
Stop at the first difficulty
Not quite. The article says: Work to the full, but when stress sets in, recognise that your natural limit has been reached.
questions.rationale: “‘Stress is our limit’ makes much more sense… when we feel that we have fallen victim to stress we should know that we have reached our limits.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, do people see deaths every day and yet miss their meaning?
options: They believe the dead will return
Not quite. The article says: They think of each person only in worldly terms and have no living picture of the next world.
They think of each person only in worldly terms and have no living picture of the next world
Well reasoned. They feel a loss, not a meeting with God.
Death is hidden from public view
Not quite. The article says: They think of each person only in worldly terms and have no living picture of the next world.
They are too frightened to look
Not quite. The article says: They think of each person only in worldly terms and have no living picture of the next world.
questions.rationale: “We see man in relation to this ephemeral world, but fail to see him in relation to the next eternal world.”
